job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today we are discussing how our country is managed. Rohan, do you think a village government works alone? Rohan: Yes, because it is their village and they make their own rules. Teacher: Actually, the village government is part of a larger system. It follows laws made by the state and national governments to ensure consistency. Priya: What about the old days with kings? Were they always cruel dictators? Teacher: Not necessarily. Some monarchs were wise and cared for their people, though they held all power. Today, we live in a democracy where we choose our leaders. Priya: Does everyone in the country get to vote? Teacher: In our democracy, we follow the principle of universal adult franchise. This means all citizens who are eighteen years or older have the right to vote, regardless of their wealth or education. It is not just about being a citizen; it is about meeting the age requirement. Rohan: So, the government is connected at all levels, and we have a say in who leads us. Teacher: Exactly. Whether it is the local panchayat or the national parliament, they work together under the same constitution to serve the people. It is a structured system where every level has a specific role to play in our daily lives.

items.evidence: It follows laws made by the state and national governments to ensure consistency.
items.q: Why does the village government follow laws made by the state and national governments?
options: So that rules stay the same everywhere
So that officials from the capital can run it
So that it only handles village festivals
So that the state makes laws for the country
items.explain: The village follows state and national laws to ensure consistency, so rules match at every level.

wrong.why: thinks the panchayat is run by officials sent from the capital
thinks the village government has no real duties
thinks the state makes laws for the whole country

items.evidence: Some monarchs were wise and cared for their people, though they held all power.
items.q: Priya thinks every king in history was a cruel dictator. What does the teacher's answer show?
options: Some kings were wise and looked after people
Some kings shared their power with the people
Some kings could be removed by angry people
Some kings were chosen by voters like today
items.explain: The teacher says some monarchs were wise and cared for people, though they still held all power.

wrong.why: misreads the sentence; kings held all power
thinks people could remove a king
thinks monarchy and democracy are the same

items.evidence: Today, we live in a democracy where we choose our leaders.
items.q: How is today's democracy different from the rule of the old kings?
options: The people pick their own leaders
The ruler holds all the power
The leader is always kind and wise
The leader is sent from the capital
items.explain: In a democracy we choose our leaders; kings held all power without being chosen.

wrong.why: reverses the two and describes a monarchy
thinks the difference is only about kindness or cruelty
thinks leaders are sent by officials, not chosen

items.evidence: It is not just about being a citizen; it is about meeting the age requirement.
items.q: Meena is sixteen and already a citizen. When will she get the right to vote?
options: When she turns eighteen years old
When she becomes a citizen of India
When she finishes her school education
When her family earns enough money
items.explain: Being a citizen is not enough; she must meet the age rule of eighteen years.

wrong.why: thinks every citizen can vote, whatever their age

items.evidence: This means all citizens who are eighteen years or older have the right to vote, regardless of their wealth or education.
items.q: Two citizens over eighteen: one rich and educated, one poor and unschooled. Who can vote?
options: Both, since their age is what counts
Only the rich one, since wealth counts
Only the educated one, since schooling counts
Neither, since officials choose the leaders
items.explain: All citizens aged eighteen or older can vote, whatever their wealth or education.

wrong.why: thinks leaders are appointed by officials, not chosen by people
